title: Structured Hiring Committee and Decision Protocol
author: Jordan Kim
content:
Purpose

This page codifies the charter, membership, meeting cadence, and formal decision protocol for hiring committees across Redwood Inference. The goal is to ensure consistent, equitable, and efficient hiring decisions while preserving manager autonomy and accountability. This process applies to IC and manager hires through L6; executive / VP-level hires follow a separate executive search protocol described in the leadership hiring appendix (link at bottom).

Scope and goals

- Scope: All full-time and long-term contractor hires (>6 months) for engineering, product, data, and platform teams.
- Primary goals:
  - Reduce time-to-offer to <= 21 calendar days for priority roles.
  - Increase offer-acceptance rate to >= 75% through calibrated offers and improved candidate experience.
  - Ensure consistent application of scorecards and diversity & inclusion best practices.
  - Provide a repeatable record for audit and post-hire review.

Committee charter and membership

- Charter: Provide a cross-functional panel that validates role requirements, confirms scorecard alignment, and signs off on final offers for senior and cross-team roles. The committee is not a veto body for manager-level hiring decisions except where the role is cross-functional or above the manager's compensation band.
- Standard membership:
  1. Hiring Manager (chair) — presents role context, impact, and preferred candidate.
  2. HR Partner — ensures process compliance, EEO & compensation alignment.
  3. Peer Engineer/Product Lead — assesses on-skill fit and team dynamics.
  4. Technical Reviewer (subject matter expert) — deep technical validation.
  5. Program / Product Manager or Customer-facing stakeholder (as applicable) — for cross-functional roles.
- Optional members when needed: Security reviewer, Privacy lead, Finance approver (for unusual budget exceptions), People Ops Sr.

Decision authority and boundaries

- Hiring Manager retains primary authority up to L5 for individual contributor hires. The committee provides advisory scoring and a formal sign-off for L6+ or cross-team hires.
- Committee sign-off is required in the following scenarios:
  - Role band >= L6 (senior IC / manager level).
  - Director or manager roles that will span multiple teams.
  - Compensation requests exceeding the baseline band by >15%.
  - Roles flagged for regulatory, security, or customer-data access.

Meeting cadence and minimum artifacts

- Cadence: Standing 45-minute committee slots every Tuesday and Thursday at 10:00 PT for teams with active searches. Occasional ad-hoc reviews can be scheduled for urgent offers.
- Required artifacts submitted by Hiring Manager at least 24 hours before the meeting:
  - Completed role scorecard (template below).
  - Candidate packet: resume, interview notes, anonymized score summary, reference check summary (if available).
  - Proposed offer terms and rationale.

Scorecard template (text table)

Use this normalized scorecard to make comparisons easier across candidates. Each criterion is scored 1–5; total and comments required.

| Criterion | Weight | Score (1-5) | Weighted | Notes |
| Role-fit / impact potential | 30% | ___ | ___ | Candidate's likely contribution in first 6 months |
| Technical depth | 25% | ___ | ___ | Core technical skills and learning velocity |
| Collaboration & communication | 20% | ___ | ___ | Cross-team partnership and influence |
| Ownership & execution | 15% | ___ | ___ | Evidence of delivering end-to-end outcomes |
| Culture & values alignment | 10% | ___ | ___ | Behavioral alignment with Redwood values |
| TOTAL | 100% | | ___ |

Decision protocol (step-by-step)

1. Intake: Hiring Manager opens req in Greenhouse and attaches draft scorecard.
2. Pre-screen: HR Partner verifies role description, compensation band, and sourcing plan.
3. Interview loop: Standardized interview loop executed; interviewers submit scorecards within 48 hours.
4. Committee review: Candidate packet and composite score submitted to committee; committee meets to discuss.
5. Decision matrix applied:
   - If composite score >= 4.2: Committee recommends hire; hiring manager may extend offer after HR confirms comp and references.
   - If composite score 3.6–4.19: Committee recommends hire subject to manager justification and at least one additional reference check.
   - If composite score < 3.6: Committee recommends decline. Manager may escalate with documented rationale.
6. Compensation exceptions: Any requested comp above the band midpoint +15% requires People Ops and Finance approval before an offer is extended.
7. Final approval: HR Partner signs off on offer terms; Hiring Manager communicates offer within 48 hours of approval.

Offer approval flow and timelines

- Time targets:
  - Acceptable maximum time from final interview to offer (internal approval complete): 5 business days.
  - Target time-to-offer (final interview to verbal): 48 hours.
  - Target time-to-fill (req open to accepted start date): < 35 days for priority roles.
- Escalation: If approvals stall >72 hours, the hiring manager flags People Ops for priority routing; People Ops will convene expedited committee within 24 hours for qualified cases.

Onboarding handoff checklist (for committee to validate)

- Required artifacts at time of offer acceptance:
  - Confirmed start date and first-week agenda (manager-provided).
  - Clear role objectives for first 30/60/90 days (manager-provided).
  - Permanent hires: legal paperwork completed, payroll and benefits created.
  - IT & tools access request submitted: GitHub, Slack, internal dashboards, Google Workspace, internal CI/CD access list.
  - First-week meetings scheduled: team intro, platform orientation, security & privacy training slot.

Manager expectations: onboarding & early performance

- First 2 weeks:
  - Daily check-ins during first 5 working days.
  - Clear orientation plan with at least 3 knowledge transfer sessions.
- 30-day:
  - Manager provides written 30-day goals and schedules a 30-day feedback checkpoint.
- 60-day:
  - Progress review with focus on ownership of a defined deliverable.
- 90-day:
  - Formal 90-day hiring review: hiring manager completes a 90-day evaluation and submits it to People Ops for the talent record.

Performance and feedback rituals aligned to hiring outcomes

- Calibration: Quarterly hiring calibration sessions per department to review mid-year hiring patterns, offer accept rates, and common score distribution.
- Feedback loop: For all hires where the candidate score was within 0.2 points of the threshold or where offers were declined, the hiring manager completes a short "post-offer retrospective" form stored on the candidate record.
- New-hire NPS: People Ops sends a 30- and 120-day onboarding survey with an internal NPS target >= 60.

Metrics and KPIs maintained by People Ops

- Time-to-offer (median): target <= 21 days for priority roles.
- Time-to-fill (median): target <= 35 days for priority roles.
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 75%.
- New-hire first-year retention: target >= 90%.
- Proportion of hires needing corrective performance action in first 12 months: target <= 7%.

Equity and inclusion safeguards

- Interview anonymization: For initial resume screening, remove names and non-essential demographic identifiers when possible for high-volume roles.
- Diverse slates: Hiring managers must present at least one diverse candidate slate (as defined in Redwood sourcing guidelines) before advancing to committee for all external senior hires.
- Standardized questions & rubrics: Interviewers must use the canonical scorecard and at least two structured behavioral questions drawn from our catalog to reduce variance.

Documentation and audit trail

- All committee decisions, scorecards, and approvals are logged in the candidate's Greenhouse record and retained for 24 months for review and audit. People Ops will maintain a quarterly digest of "committee decisions vs outcomes" to identify systemic drift.

Exceptions and urgent hiring flow

- Fast-track: For time-sensitive customer-impact hires, the hiring manager may request expedited approval. Criteria for fast-track:
  - Demonstrable customer-impact or revenue risk within 30 days.
  - Written justification attached to the req.
- Fast-track process:
  - HR Partner confirms eligibility and convenes an ad-hoc mini-committee (hiring manager, HR Partner, one technical reviewer) with a target decision time of 24 hours.

Appendix: Templates and links

- Role scorecard template (copyable) — attach this page.
- Offer approval matrix (spreadsheet) — People Ops shared drive link.
- New hire 30/60/90 template — templates/docs/onboarding-templates.
- Leadership hiring appendix — contact People Ops senior recruiter for access.

Ownership and review cadence

- Owner: People Ops (process owner: Jordan Kim).
- Review cycle: Annual review in Q4 or earlier if metrics show process drift.
- Change control: Any changes to decision thresholds or committee makeup require People Ops and two stakeholder approvals (Engineering Head and HR Director).

Contact

- For questions or to request an exception, email people-ops@redwood.ai and CC your HR Partner.
